audit.whatIsWrong: The chart handed Lucian Levels 4-5, first item and 2+ items while the prose in the same file says the exact opposite ('his health and stored-W smash out-grit you', 'Sett out-stats you flatly', 'he hard out-scales you'), and the Emerald+ figure is 33.33%.
audit.why: The packet chart (Lucian, Skill, Sett, Sett, Skill, Sett, Skill) already matches every why[] line word for word — the chart layer simply never caught up. Level 1 is Lucian's (auto range plus the Lightslinger double-tap before Pit Grit alternates); from 3 onward Grit and Haymaker take over.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Lucian / Skill / Sett / Sett / Skill / Sett / Skill in both layers, with ratings and difficulty prose brought down to match.

audit.why: Four spikes present and honest: Lvl 1-2 Lucian window, Lvl 6 The Show Stopper, 'His W' Haymaker return, 2+ items Sett scaling. They are stated as Sett's spikes, which is right in a 33% matchup.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two decisive interactions never reach the full layer: Haymaker (W) converts the damage you deal into a shield plus a true-damage punch, and The Show Stopper (R) grounds.
audit.why: Riot text on W: 'Sett passively stores damage he takes as Grit. On cast, Sett expends all stored Grit to gain a shield and punch an area, dealing true damage in the center.' The shield eats Lucian's entire burst window, which is the flagged missing interaction for this matchup. R carries the grounding flag, so Relentless Pursuit is not an answer to the grab — Flash is. Both were absent everywhere in full.
audit.corrected: Haymaker shield written into report[5].t and phases[5].why; the grounding into dosFull[2].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: Facebreaker was described only as 'the pull-stun'. It stuns only when enemies are on opposite sides of Sett; alone on one side you are slowed instead.
audit.why: Riot text: 'Sett pulls in all enemies on opposite sides of him... If enemies were only on one side, they are slowed instead of stunned.' The existing 'stay off the line between him and units' advice was right but never explained, so a player cannot tell when the button is actually lethal. Range 490, cooldown 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s.
audit.corrected: Precondition and numbers written into breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d and phases[3].why.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.difficulty and report[14].t both read 'Favoured matchup' while diff is HARD and the win rate is 33.33%.
audit.why: A page that says HARD in one field and 'Favoured' in another is unreadable.
audit.corrected: Both changed to 'Hard matchup', carry threat raised to 7/10.

edits.before: Full kit: Q-AA-E-AA-W-AA strings chunk a third of his HP. Trade on every CS he takes from the wrong angle.
edits.after: Grit catches up: every auto you sink in fills Haymaker, and he hands it back as true damage your resists cannot stop.

edits.before: Keep the pressure rolling but track Facebreaker — your lead is HP-bar bullying, not all-in math, until items arrive.
edits.after: His HP and a loaded Haymaker out-grit you — Facebreaker is 16s at rank 1 and stuns only with minions on his far side.

edits.before: First item spike is your kill window — the dash-weave combo now deletes half bars. Force the issue before he stabilizes.
edits.after: His first item out-stats you flatly — the Haymaker shield eats your burst window and Pit Grit regen heals back the rest.

edits.before: - Sett Facebreaker: matchup-defining — The pull-stun starts his combo — stay off the line between him and units. It governs your forward steps. - E dash spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Sett Facebreaker: 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s at 490 range — it only stuns with targets on opposite sides, so stay off the line between him and his minions and it is just a slow. - E spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.

edits.before: The pull-stun starts his combo — stay off the line between him and units. Commit on its cooldown, never into it.
edits.after: Facebreaker only stuns with units on his far side — off that line it is just a slow. It is 16s at rank 1.

edits.before: Sett spends Facebreaker early — the closest thing this matchup has to a guarantee.
edits.after: The Show Stopper grounds you — E cannot answer it, so keep Flash for his 400-range grab.

edits.before: Track Sett’s Facebreaker: The pull-stun starts his combo — stay off the line between him and units. Forward steps wait for its downtime.
edits.after: Haymaker (W) shields him with the damage you deal — bait it out empty before you commit, or your whole burst window is absorbed.

edits.before: Favoured matchup — difficulty 4/10, Sett carry threat 5/10.
edits.after: Hard matchup — difficulty 7/10, Sett carry threat 7/10.
